docs.title: PySATL Experiment
docs.text: PySATL is a free and open source statistics library written in Python, designed to support all major researcher demands for statistical experiments.

docs.title: Quick-Start
docs.text: Follow the 4-step experimental workflow in experiment_example/Quick-Start_Template.md.

docs.title: Available Experiment Types
docs.text:
• critical_value - Calculate critical values for statistical tests
  • power - Evaluate statistical power of tests
  • time_complexity - Measure performance and time complexity
  • generation_only - Generate samples without statistical evaluation

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: PySATL Experiment provides a structured 4-step workflow for statistical experiment design, evaluation, and optimization. The system is designed to be modular, allowing researchers to mix and match different experiment types based on their specific needs.

docs.title: Experiment Types
docs.text: The framework supports four distinct experiment types, each serving a specific purpose:

docs.title: 1. Critical Value Analysis
docs.text:
Purpose: Calculate critical values for statistical tests given a significance level (alpha) and distribution.

Use case: Determining the threshold at which a test statistic would lead to rejection of the null hypothesis.

Configuration: Uses normal_critical_values.json with parameters for distribution, significance level, and degrees of freedom.

docs.title: 2. Power Evaluation
docs.text:
Purpose: Evaluate the statistical power of tests to detect effects of a given size.

Use case: Planning experiments to ensure sufficient sample size for detecting meaningful effects.

Configuration: Uses normal_power.json with parameters for effect size, sample size, significance level, and power target.

docs.title: 3. Time Complexity Measurement
docs.text:
Purpose: Measure the performance and time complexity of experiment execution.

Use case: Profiling and optimizing experiment pipelines for large-scale studies.

Configuration: Uses normal_time_complexity.json with parameters for number of iterations, dataset sizes, and measurement parameters.

docs.title: 4. Generation Only
docs.text:
Purpose: Generate samples or data without performing statistical evaluation.

Use case: Rapid prototyping, data generation for testing, or creating baseline datasets.

Configuration: Uses normal_generation_only.json with parameters for sample generation method and output format.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The standard workflow follows these steps in sequence:

  1. Calculate Critical Values - Establish the statistical thresholds
  2. Evaluate Power - Assess the ability to detect effects
  3. Measure Time Complexity - Profile performance characteristics
  4. Generation Only - Create samples/data as needed

Each step can be run independently using poetry run experiment build-and-run <step_number>_<step_name>.

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
All experiment configurations are stored in experiment_example/configs/<experiment_type>/ and follow a consistent JSON structure with the following common fields:

  • hypothesis - The statistical hypothesis being tested
  • distribution - The assumed data distribution
  • criteria - Evaluation criteria/tests
  • parameters - Experiment-specific parameters

docs.title: Extension Points
docs.text:
New experiment types can be added by:

  1. Creating a new configuration directory under experiment_example/configs/
  2. Adding a corresponding step in the Quick-Start template
  3. Updating the CLI to handle the new step number
  4. Adding documentation for the new experiment type

docs.title: Running experiments in Docker
docs.text:
This image ships a self-contained CLI (experiment): code + dependencies, no local install needed. You type commands in your host terminal, they execute inside the container — the same pattern as trader terminals (e.g. freqtrade): host terminal → docker compose run --rm <service> <subcommand>.

Docker Hub namespace (temporary) — there is no pysatl organization on Docker Hub yet, so the image is temporarily published from a contributor's personal account. Pull commands below use the placeholder <dockerhub-username> — do not substitute a real account name. Target name after org creation: pysatl/pysatl-experiment (see issue #1; pull commands by pysatl/… appear only after that issue is closed).

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
docker pull <dockerhub-username>/pysatl-experiment:latest
mkdir -p user_data
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/user_data:/app/user_data" \
  <dockerhub-username>/pysatl-experiment:latest --help

With compose (service already mounts ./user_data):

mkdir -p user_data
docker compose run --rm pysatl-experiment --help

docs.title: Full scenario
docs.text:
docker compose run --rm pysatl-experiment create my-exp
docker compose run --rm pysatl-experiment configure my-exp \
  -cr KS \
  -l 0.05 -l 0.01 \
  -s 100 -s 200 \
  -c 1000 \
  -h normal \
  -expt critical_value \
  -con sqlite:///user_data/pysatl.sqlite
docker compose run --rm pysatl-experiment show my-exp
docker compose run --rm pysatl-experiment build-and-run my-exp

The quick-start scenario above mirrors the local one in README.md and experiment_example/Quick-Start_Template.md. If you prefer running natively (without Docker), see the local quick start there.

Notes:

  • Command names use dashes: build-and-run, not build_and_run.
  • configure --connection is required. Inside the container always pass sqlite:///user_data/<name>.sqlite so the DB lands in the mounted volume.
  • Logs go to stderr by default; add --log-file user_data/<name>.log to build-and-run to keep them. Example configs live in experiment_example/configs/.

docs.title: Where the data lives
docs.text:
Everything is in one folder: ./user_data on the host, mounted at /app/user_data in the container (docker-compose.yml).

Artifact Path on host Experiment configs user_data/.experiments/<name>.json Reports (PDF) user_data/.results/<report>.pdf SQLite databases user_data/*.sqlite Logs (if --log-file used) user_data/<name>.log

Data survives docker rm. Nothing valuable is written to the container layer: configs, reports and the DB sit in the volume. Verify it: run an experiment, remove the container, run again — the results are still there.

Do not override the workdir (docker run -w <dir>): the image and compose pin WORKDIR /app, and the sqlite:///user_data/... paths are relative to it.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Default is SQLite in the volume: sqlite:///user_data/pysatl.sqlite. The legacy code default (AbstractDbStore) points there as well.

Power experiments need critical values first. The checker reads the limit_distributions table, so before a power run either execute a critical_value experiment against the same DB file first, or copy a populated DB into user_data/. Without it the power run fails with ConnectionError.

To use an external database, pass any SQLAlchemy URL via configure --connection, e.g. postgresql://user:pass@host/db. No code changes needed.

docs.title: Migration from the old default
docs.text:
If you ran the project before and have a database in the repo root, move it into user_data/ so the new default (sqlite:///user_data/...) picks it up:

mkdir -p user_data
mv pysatl.sqlite user_data/          # if present
mv training_samples.sqlite user_data/ # if present (generation_only runs)

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tag Meaning latest Last stable release. edge Last main commit. May be unstable. vX.Y.Z A specific release. main-<sha> A specific commit (edge builds only).

docs.title: Deployment (TODO)
docs.text:
• GitHub repository secrets: DOCKERHUB_USERNAME (your Docker Hub login) and DOCKERHUB_TOKEN (access token with Read & Write, not the password). Configure at GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions.
  • CI pushes to <dockerhub-username>/pysatl-experiment on push to main (edge) and on releases (latest).
  • Smoke check (temporary name): docker pull <dockerhub-username>/pysatl-experiment:latest + docker run --rm <dockerhub-username>/pysatl-experiment:latest --help.
  • issue #1 — migrate publish target to pysatl/pysatl-experiment after the pysatl organization exists on Docker Hub; then update docs/docker.md and README.md (replace <dockerhub-username> with pysatl). Until then, do not use pysatl/… in pull commands.
